name: Spice Girls
editorial_article: The Spice Girls were a defining British girl group of the 1990s, becoming one of the most commercially successful music acts in history. Formed in London in 1994, the group consisted of Mel B ("Scary Spice"), Melanie C ("Sporty Spice"), Emma Bunton ("Baby Spice"), Geri Halliwell ("Ginger Spice"), and Victoria Beckham ("Posh Spice"). With their infectious dance-pop sound and the empowering "Girl Power" slogan, the group transcended music to become a worldwide cultural phenomenon, synonymous with the "Cool Britannia" era of the late 20th century. \n\nTheir debut single, "Wannabe" (1996), catapulted them to international stardom, topping the charts in 37 countries and laying the foundation for their debut album, *Spice* (1996). *Spice* remains the best-selling album by a female group in history, having sold over 23 million copies worldwide. They followed this massive success with *Spiceworld* (1997) and the R&B-inflected *Forever* (2000). Beyond the charts, their impact on pop culture was profound; they redefined the template for girl groups, influenced the teen pop resurgence of the decade, and became symbols of a specifically British brand of feminism that resonated globally. Despite internal changes—most notably Geri Halliwell’s departure in 1998—and several hiatuses, the group has reunited periodically for highly successful global tours, proving the enduring legacy of their sound and message. Their contribution to music and celebrity culture is widely recognized, having secured numerous awards, including the Brit Award for Outstanding Contribution to Music.

editorial_bio: The Spice Girls were a seminal British girl group formed in 1994, known for pioneering the 'Girl Power' phenomenon and becoming the best-selling girl group of all time. Defining the 1990s teen pop resurgence, the group achieved massive international success with hits like 'Wannabe' before embarking on successful solo careers and periodic high-profile reunions.
